correctness.rationale: For matching samples, the observed coordinate matrices have mutually orthogonal left and right singular vectors, so singular-value shrinkage acts componentwise. The exact scalar recurrence yields activation at \(\lfloor\tau/(\delta s_j)\rfloor+2\), after which the error is multiplied by \(1-\delta\). The activation bound gives error magnitude below \(s_j\), and \(|1-\delta|<1\) prevents deactivation. The \(\delta=1\) integer/noninteger cases give the stated settling index. A spectral-norm dual certificate and strict Frobenius equality prove uniqueness of the finite-\(\tau\) regularized minimizer. The packaged exact-rational checker returns VERIFY_OK.

value.rationale: The original SVT paper singles out empirical nondecreasing rank as a practical reason the method is efficient. Matching observations form the simplest sparse observation graph with exactly orthogonal singular directions, so they are a mathematically natural test class rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem gives a complete rank-entry schedule, proves persistence of activated directions, identifies the exact finite-termination resonance at \(\delta=1\), and supplies a closed-form implementation benchmark that isolates the effect lost when observation edges begin to share rows or columns.
